title: HŌICHI THE EARLESS
subtitle: the musician who played for the dead
source: Lafcadio Hearn, Kwaidan (1904), 'The Story of Mimi-nashi-Hoichi'; Amidaji = today's Akama Shrine, Shimonoseki (Hoichi Hall statue); Battle of Dan-no-ura 1185

lines.say: [nervous whisper] Kon... why does that statue have no ears?
[low] A ghost ripped them off.
Centuries ago, a blind musician named Hōichi lived at a temple by the sea.
cap: lived at a temple by the sea.

lines.say: Every night, he sang of Dan-no-ura, the sea battle where the Heike clan drowned.
One night, a samurai in armor came for him.
cap: a {r:samurai} in armor came for him.

lines.say: [deep, ghostly] Hoichi. My lord wishes to hear you.
He was led to a grand hall full of nobles. He played until dawn, and they wept.
cap: He was led to a {o:grand hall}

lines.say: Night after night, he went back. So the priest had him followed...
cap: Night after night, he went back.

lines.say: There was no hall.
He was playing alone in a graveyard, surrounded by ghost fires.
[horrified] He was playing for GHOSTS?!
To hide him, the priest painted holy sutras over every inch of his body.
cap: over every inch of his body.

lines.say: Ghosts can't see what the sutras cover.
That night, the samurai came back.
[ghostly whisper] Hoichi... where are you?
Nothing. Just two ears, floating in the dark.
[grim] They forgot his ears.
So the ghost took the only part of Hōichi it could see.
Hōichi lived, and became the most famous singer in Japan: Hōichi the Earless.
cap: and became the most famous singer in Japan:

lines.say: His statue still sits at Akama Shrine, in Shimonoseki.
[nervous] Kon... who's clapping?
